lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\FaceRecognition\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
1 class in lib/ whose name does not follow PSR-4 below OCA\FaceRecognition, the namespace the server derives from <namespace> of info.xml. The loader of the server does not find such a class.
13 uses of the private API of the server in 9 files. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

Nothing in the app calls 1 route outside OCS. Looked for: a route name or a path in the PHP source and the templates, in 6 files of the frontend source and in the navigation of info.xml. The frontend puts the path of the app and the rest of a URL together at run time, so every text there that reads like a path below the app counted as a call. A route stays behind when the frontend stops calling it. A route that only a client outside the app calls shows here as well, unless its method allows requests from other origins (CORS).

psalm/phar, phpunit/phpunit are in require-dev of composer.json. The manual recommends a vendor-bin/ of bamarni/composer-bin-plugin per tool, so that the dependencies of a tool cannot conflict with those of the app.

8 inline styles in templates/. The default Content Security Policy of the server allows inline style; a response whose policy disallows it drops them. A stylesheet added with OCP\Util::addStyle() holds in both cases.

3 transactions are opened and closed by hand. The trait TTransactional has atomic() since Nextcloud 24 and atomicRetry() since Nextcloud 27, which repeats a transaction that ran into a deadlock, as the manual recommends.
lib/ reads the clock directly in 9 places. OCP\AppFramework\Utility\ITimeFactory, a PSR-20 ClockInterface, gives the same time and can be replaced in a test.

The app reads and writes its app config in 22 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.

Nothing in the app calls 2 routes outside OCS whose method allows requests from other origins (CORS), or that answer the preflight of such a request (OPTIONS). They are there for clients outside the app, so this is no defect in itself.
2 public methods of controllers are reached by no route.
The app has 2 OCS routes and no openapi.json. Clients of OCS are generated from such a specification, and nothing else tells them what these routes take and return.
